glossary.definition: An event that could have caused harm but did not.
A rating set from the level of harm, actual or potential, defined by the organization.
An action taken to remove the cause of an incident so it does not recur.
The role accountable for decisions and records in a defined workflow.
An event that caused harm, damage, or a stoppage.
A condition someone noticed before any event occurred.
Statements that a software demonstration can prove or fail to prove, derived from the plant's own problem statement, process map, and decision table.
A step in the reporting process after which no record shows a decision was made, leaving a report unresolved.

example.label: Illustrative example
example.description: An unnamed Canadian manufacturer evaluates incident and near-miss reporting software for one production area; all situations and records are hypothetical, not customer results.

reviewedChapters.title: Map how incidents and near-misses are reported today
reviewedChapters.summary: The page maps the current-state incident and near-miss reporting workflow across four subsections that match the plan exactly. All factual claims about ICC Safety capabilities are correctly framed as published descriptions requiring demonstration confirmation. The Ontario JHSC source is cited only where Ontario-specific regulatory content is discussed, with an explicit caution against assuming those rules apply nationally. Workflow elements (role, input, decision, record, exception) are present in each subsection. Illustrative examples are labeled and use an unnamed Canadian manufacturer. No FAQ section appears, which is correct because the plan assigns none. The changed paragraph correctly presents ICC Safety page content as a vendor problem description rather than measured data. No previous findings were raised. Links use the two supplied source URLs plus an allowed internal path. No scope boundary violations were detected.
decisions: Decide what counts as an incident, a near-miss, and a hazard report
Decide whether a report is accepted into the log
Decide whether corrective action is required
Decide which steps are required and which are habit
Assign a named owner and a backup to each decision
Decide which steps the software must support first
